- **Input:** the task file at alys `main` (origin/main), commit `24c83518ba2180e9d8236361ee96f2c138170daa`, read through the board's own parser from that checkout; per-week counts only.
- **Window:** 60 days, 2026-09-11 to 2026-11-09; the game is taken to start on the first day.
- **Kept per order:** dates, Pn, tier, program, the Options and Steps counts, difficulty, the board's score. Every title, step, option and Say line was dropped at the parse; a private row kept its dates and Pn only, so a private decision is modelled as a close.
- **Rows:** 102 open and 96 done (no Done row has left the file; its first ticks fall in the window's third week, so the first weeks show no close); 26 rows are private, counted in the totals and never shown apart or named; 0 done rows had no readable date and were skipped.
- **Ambiguous rows:** 78 done rows carry neither a `Project:` line nor a private mark (ticked before stamping began). 72 were resolved public from the sections they sat in across 247 versions of the file; 6 never showed in a public section, or sat in a private one, and are counted private.
- **Stated cadence:** a stated game cadence: ten lessons and three lifts a week, on an invented spread. It is a schedule the sim assumes, not a read of anyone's learning record, and it assumes every lesson and lift lands; a region is a stated week of ten lessons.
- **Ground model:** expected value, not the map: a pylon adds half its disc (4.0 tiles); the blight is the siege's size (`tiles_per_attacker`, clamped); the night spread (`spread_base + spread_per_day × day`, capped) takes wild tiles only. Scrap from play (ambient nodes, kills, habitats) is not modelled; only evidence caches are.

| # | Target | Result | Number |

| 1 | A median day funds one pylon, or one turret and a habitat | **met** | 6 cells on the median day (needs 4) |
| 2 | A good week grows the ground by a ring; a quiet week takes no built tile | **met** | 3 good weeks (ten or more closes and decisions); the leanest grew 24 tiles short of a ring because the free ground ran out · the map's free ground is used up on day 51 · 2 weeks with no close (the spread takes wild tiles only, by rule) |
| 3 | The siege is legible: the blight follows the backlog (held at either clamp or squeezed by a full map on under a quarter of the days) | **met** | 11 of 60 days held at a clamp or squeezed · attackers 2–78 (78 today) · largest wave 38 |
| 4 | Level 5 within the first month and level 10 within the quarter, so the module card is a monthly-ish event | **met** | level 6 at day 30 · 10 projected at day 90 · level 5 on day 18 · level 10 on day — |

**On real closes alone** (no stated lessons or lifts): target 1 not met (0 cells on the median day), target 4 not met (level 5 at day 30, 8 projected at day 90). Targets 1 and 4 lean on the stated cadence; 2 and 3 are the backlog's.

**Ground is an upper bound.** The sim takes every pylon to stand. In the prototype a machine can destroy a pylon at night and its ground goes wild again (version 2's rule, kept): that is a design question, recorded with D33 in the design repo.

## The arc, in plain words

**The first week.** By the seventh day the evidence of that week has landed 26 cells, enough for 3 pylons; the Keeper is level 1 and the ground stands at about 11% of the map. The blight at the edges is 16 tiles, drawn from 8 orders at the walls, and a night brings 20 machines. **The first month.** At day 30 the Keeper is level 6 (level 5 came on day 18), the ground is about 46% and the blight 52 tiles; 4 regions are mapped on the stated cadence. **The quarter.** At the window's pace the Keeper would reach level 10 by day 90 (projected; the file holds 60 days). On the last day of the window the ground is about 64%, the blight 143 tiles from 78 attackers, and a night is 38 machines.

## Tuning

Every change is a rules-file edit (`rules/fieldworks.json`), never the engine. Each row was applied in order and the whole sim re-run; the columns are the four targets after that row (✓ met, ✗ not).

| Step | Key | Before → after | Why | T1 | T2 | T3 | T4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | the v1 rules | — | the baseline | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| 1 | `fortress.blight.tiles_per_attacker` | 5 → 2 | With 78 attackers today the upper clamp held the blight on 26 of 60 days, so a close did not visibly move it; at 2 the upper clamp binds on no day, though the lower clamp still holds the thin early weeks (step 8) and a filling map squeezes it (step 7). | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| 2 | `fortress.waves.per_attacker` | 1 → 0.25 | One machine per attacker made a night 80+ machines on the real backlog; a quarter keeps the backlog legible in the wave without swamping it. | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| 3 | `fortress.waves.max` | null → 40 | The performance budget (GDD §3.3) is 40 machines on a phone; the wave never exceeds it. | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| 4 | `fortress.waves.per_day_cap_days` | null → 7 | Under the real-day clock (D25) the day count grows without end; the day term stops growing after a week, so night 60 is not three times night 20. | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| 5 | `xp.player_step` | 100 → 200 | At 100 the Keeper reached level 10 on day 43, about a level every four days; at 200 level 5 lands on day 18 and level 10 is projected for day 90, the quarter. | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| 6 | `fortress.costs.pylon.cells` | 4 → 8 | On the real pace the stated lessons alone bought seven pylons a week and the map's free ground ran out on day 15 (day 17 after steps 1–5), after which the blight could no longer show the backlog. A pylon at 8 cells is two lesson days; a median day still funds a turret and a habitat (4 cells). | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| 7 | `fortress.pylon_reach` | 2.6 → 1.6 | With the cost doubled the map still filled by day 22. A shorter reach makes each pylon about 4 new tiles, so half the ground (the run's win, D30) arrives around day 30 and the free ground lasts to day 51. | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| 8 | `fortress.blight.min_tiles` | 24 → 8 | Counted honestly, the lower clamp held the blight on 13 of the early days, when only a handful of orders were old enough to attack, so a close there moved nothing. At 8 the floor still draws a thin edge of blight and the blight follows the backlog on 49 of 60 days. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

**Not touched:** the engine; rarity, XP bases and multipliers, medals, the skill step, the siege's ages and weights (they are the design's definition of an attacker, not a balance knob), the other structure costs and every structure's health, the machines, the modules, the caches by grade and by kind, and the explore block.
